Five scripts.
One aperture.

The APER axis carries the lotus-gateway idea from Malayalam into four more Indian scripts. One variable system, one spectrum, one build pipeline — with each script's own shaping and metrics.

01 / Scripts

The same idea,
four grammars.

Move the APER slider above and every script below follows. Devanagari keeps its shirorekha straight while the counters open; Telugu and Kannada take the full loop treatment; Tamil stays gentler.

02 / Axis

Round → Bloom → Petal

The transform moves existing TrueType points, never adds or removes them, so every intermediate APER value is a designed, point-compatible master.

In context

04 / Download

Files

Each script ships as a variable Regular and Bold, static Round/Petal instances, and COLRv1 Spectrum builds. WOFF2 for the web, TTF for desktop and print.

ScriptVariableStaticSpectrum
Devanagari TTF · WOFF2 Round · Petal · Bold Petal Bold · Regular
Tamil TTF · WOFF2 Round · Petal · Bold Petal Bold · Regular
Telugu TTF · WOFF2 Round · Petal · Bold Petal Bold · Regular
Kannada TTF · WOFF2 Round · Petal · Bold Petal Bold · Regular

Derivative model. The Malayalam branch is a derivative of Manjari. The Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada branches are derivatives of the corresponding Noto Sans faces. The aperture engine, APER axis, Spectrum treatment, metrics and specimens are original work by the Ezhuthu Project Authors. All bases are used under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.

Independence. This project is independent and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google, the Noto Project Authors, Sarvam AI, or SMC. The blue → orange spectrum is an homage to Sarvam's visual language.

Script notes. Devanagari uses an absolute freeze at the headline so the shirorekha never bends. Tamil uses a gentler profile because its counters are fewer and more open. Telugu and Kannada take the full hole-and-crown warp, where their round loops carry the petal most naturally.

Technical. Every master is point-compatible. The build is deterministic: repeated runs produce byte-identical TTF and WOFF2 files. Fonts are subset-free and retain the full upstream coverage, including conjuncts, reph forms, matras and Vedic extensions where the base supports them.
